report:
**Conclusion**
The claim is **true**: abaloparatide significantly reduces the risk of new vertebral fractures in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.

**Evidence Summary**
Primary evidence comes from the landmark Phase 3 ACTIVE (Abaloparatide Comparator Trial in Vertebral Endpoints) randomized clinical trial. In this 18-month study of over 2,400 postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, daily subcutaneous injections of abaloparatide (80 µg) produced an 86% relative risk reduction in new morphometric vertebral fractures compared to placebo (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2544640). Comparative evaluations demonstrate that abaloparatide substantially lowers vertebral fracture incidence and increases bone mineral density compared with placebo (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11954689/).

Based on these results, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved abaloparatide (brand name Tymlos) in 2017 for treating postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at high risk for fracture (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208743lbl.pdf). Subsequent systematic reviews and meta-analyses consistently confirm that abaloparatide significantly reduces the risk of vertebral fractures compared to placebo (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00198-019-04947-2). Robust clinical trial data and regulatory evaluations confirm that abaloparatide is an effective treatment for preventing vertebral fractures in postmenopausal osteoporosis.
